definition_zh: 锚；使固定；新闻主播；（精神上的）支柱
definition_en: a heavy device dropped from a boat to hold it in place, the act of fixing something firmly, or a person who presents the news
core_image: 一只铁锚沉入海底，缆绳绷紧，船停住了
scene: 风浪里，船长把船开到海湾，抛下锚等天亮。They anchored the boat in the bay until the storm passed.
sceneCN: 这里 anchor 是「抛锚；使固定」（第 2 个义项：作动词，用锚把船固定住）；句意是他们把船停在湾里抛锚，直到风暴过去。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：未固定的；无依无靠的

senses.title: The device that holds a ship
senses.definition: a heavy metal object dropped from a ship so that its weight and grip on the seabed hold the ship in place
senses.definitionCN: 从船上沉入水底的重金属物，凭重量与抓力把船固定在原处
senses.example: The ship let down its anchor outside the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 船在港口外抛下了锚。
senses.why: The word came into English from Greek and Latin names for the same iron hook, so the object has kept its name for more than a thousand years.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经由希腊语与拉丁语中指同一铁钩的名称进入英语，所以这个物件一千多年来都叫同一个名字。

senses.title: To fix something in place
senses.definition: to hold a boat or an object firmly in one position
senses.definitionCN: 把船或物体牢牢固定在某个位置
senses.example: They anchored the boat in the bay until the storm passed.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把船停在海湾里抛锚，直到风暴过去。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb because anchoring is an action, and from boats the verb spread to any object fixed firmly to the ground.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，是因为「抛锚」是一个动作；从船只开始，这个动词扩展到任何被牢牢固定在地面的物体。

senses.title: A mainstay or news presenter
senses.definition: a person who gives stability to a group or programme, especially the presenter who holds a news broadcast together
senses.definitionCN: 给团体或节目提供稳定性的人，尤指串联整档新闻的主播
senses.example: She has been the anchor of the evening news for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 她主持晚间新闻已经十年了。
senses.why: A news anchor holds a programme in place the way an anchor holds a ship, and the same metaphor extends to a family's steady centre.
senses.whyCN: 新闻主播稳住一档节目，就像锚稳住一艘船；同样的比喻也延伸到家庭中那个稳定的中心人物。

intro.en: Anchor is an ancient sea word, borrowed from Greek through Latin and into Old English.
intro.cn: anchor 是古老的航海词，经拉丁语从希腊语借入古英语。

items.en: ankyra meant 'anchor', and it is also the source of the medical word ankylosis.
items.cn: ankyra 意为「锚」，也是医学术语 ankylosis 的来源。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as ancora, the term used by sailors.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 ancora，是水手使用的说法。

items.en: Old English took the word from Latin and used it for the iron hook.
items.cn: 古英语从拉丁语借入 ancor，指铁锚。

items.en: The spelling shifted towards anchor under Latin influence.
items.cn: 在拉丁语影响下，拼写逐渐变为 anchor。

items.en: The figurative senses grew in broadcasting and in everyday talk about stability.
items.cn: 比喻义在广播行业与日常谈「稳定」时发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sea root; the near-meaning group gives mooring and support words.
note.cn: 形近组共享航海词根；近义组给出停泊与支撑类词。

definition_zh: 古代的；古老的；古人（复数名词）
definition_en: belonging to the distant past, extremely old, or the people who lived in ancient times
core_image: 阳光下断成几截的石柱，浮雕已被风磨平
scene: 博物馆里，孩子们围着一尊三千年前的石像听讲解。The museum displays pottery from ancient Egypt.
sceneCN: 这里 ancient 是「古代的」（第 1 个义项：属于遥远的过去）；句意是博物馆展出古埃及的陶器。

derivatives.zh: 名词：古代；古物，同源于拉丁语「在前」
名词：古董；形容词：古老的
名词：祖先，同源于拉丁语「在前」

senses.title: Of the distant past
senses.definition: belonging to the period of history before the Middle Ages, especially Greece and Rome
senses.definitionCN: 属于中世纪以前的历史时期，尤指希腊与罗马
senses.example: The museum displays pottery from ancient Egypt.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出古埃及的陶器。
senses.why: The Latin word behind it means 'before', so ancient marks what belongs to the time that came before the familiar eras of history.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁词意为「在前的」，所以 ancient 标示属于我们熟悉的历史时期之前那个时代的事物。

senses.title: Very old
senses.definition: having existed for a very long time, used of things, customs, or institutions
senses.definitionCN: 已存在很久，用于事物、习俗或制度
senses.example: The village keeps an ancient custom of lighting fires in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄保留着春天点火的古老习俗。
senses.why: Because 'before' can be measured from the speaker rather than from an era, ancient also simply means older than memory, even without a date.
senses.whyCN: 因为「在前」可以从说话人而非某个时代来量度，所以 ancient 也可以只表示比记忆更久远，不必有确切年代。

senses.title: The people of old
senses.definition: the people who lived in ancient times, especially their writers and thinkers
senses.definitionCN: 生活在古代的人，尤指其中的作家与思想家
senses.example: The ancients knew the stars better than we often assume.
senses.exampleCN: 古人对星辰的了解比我们通常以为的更多。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun for the people it describes, a common shift that lets English speak of the ancients as a collective.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成指其所描述之人的名词，这是常见的转变，使英语可以用 the ancients 统称古人。

intro.en: Ancient began as a French word for 'before', and its final -t was added by mistake.
intro.cn: ancient 最初是法语中表示「在先」的词，词尾的 -t 是后来误加上的。

items.en: ante meant 'before', in both space and time.
items.cn: ante 意为「在前」，可指空间也可指时间。

items.en: ancien meant 'old, former, belonging to earlier times'.
items.cn: ancien 意为「旧的、从前的、属于早先时代的」。

items.en: English borrowed the word as auncient, later spelled ancient.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入为 auncient，后来拼作 ancient。

items.en: The final -t was added by analogy with words such as pageant and tyrant.
items.cn: 词尾 -t 是仿照 pageant、tyrant 等词加上的。

items.en: Ancient now covers both the classical past and anything extremely old.
items.cn: 现代 ancient 既指古典时代，也指任何极其古老的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the 'before' root; the near-meaning group grades age.
note.cn: 形近组共享「在前」词根；近义组按年代远近分级。

definition_zh: adj. 轶事的；基于个别传闻的（非系统证据）
definition_en: Based on personal accounts or isolated stories rather than on systematic study or measurement.
core_image: 几个人讲的故事，凑不出一张统计图
scene: 他说这药有效，可依据只是邻居的几句话。The evidence for the remedy is purely anecdotal.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：这里说的不是「趣闻」，而是证据性质——只有个别口述，没有系统测量，所以是传闻性证据。

forms.label: 无 -er/-est 形式（多音节形容词，用 more/most）

senses.title: Of the nature of a short story
senses.definition: consisting of short, entertaining accounts of particular incidents
senses.definitionCN: 由对个别事件的简短有趣叙述构成的
senses.example: His memoir is warm and anecdotal rather than analytical.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回忆录温暖而多轶事，而非分析性的。
senses.why: The noun anecdote once meant an unpublished secret account, so the adjective still carries the sense of a private story told aloud.
senses.whyCN: 名词 anecdote 原指未公开的秘闻，所以这个形容词仍带着「私下讲出来的故事」这层意味。

senses.title: Of evidence that is not systematic
senses.definition: resting on isolated reports rather than on controlled measurement, and therefore weak as proof
senses.definitionCN: 依据零散口述而非受控测量，因而作为证明力度不足
senses.example: Anecdotal evidence cannot establish a causal link.
senses.exampleCN: 传闻性证据无法确立因果关系。
senses.why: In research writing the word is a warning label: the stories may be true, but they were not collected in a way that lets you generalise.
senses.whyCN: 在研究写作中这个词是一个警示标签：那些故事也许是真的，但收集方式不足以让你推广结论。

intro.en: Anecdotal is the adjective of anecdote, from Greek anekdota, things not published, from an-, not, and ekdotos, given out. Procopius used it for his secret history of Justinian.
intro.cn: anecdotal 是 anecdote 的形容词，anecdote 来自希腊语 anekdota「未公开之事」，由 an-「不」与 ekdotos「发布出去的」构成。普罗科匹乌斯用它称呼自己那部关于查士丁尼的秘史。

items.en: Greek an- means not or without before a vowel, the same prefix seen in anaerobic and anarchy.
items.cn: 希腊语 an- 在元音前意为「不、没有」，与 anaerobic、anarchy 中的前缀相同。

items.en: Greek ekdotos meant given out or published, from ekdidonai, to give out. The core image is handing a text over to the public.
items.cn: 希腊语 ekdotos 意为「发布出去的、出版的」，来自 ekdidonai「给出、发布」。核心意象是把一份文本交到公众手上。

items.en: Anekdota therefore meant unpublished things. Procopius gave that title to the secret account he kept back from official publication.
items.cn: 因此 anekdota 意为「未公开之事」。普罗科匹乌斯把这个名字给了他那部未正式公开的秘史。

items.en: French anecdote and then English anecdote shifted the sense from a secret account to a short entertaining story about a real incident.
items.cn: 法语 anecdote 与随后的英语 anecdote 把含义从「秘闻」转为「关于真实事件的简短有趣故事」。

items.en: Anecdotal is built with -al, and in modern research writing it labels evidence that rests on stories rather than measurement.
items.cn: anecdotal 用 -al 构成，在现代研究写作中用来标注依据故事而非测量的证据。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against antidotal, about antidotes; the near-meaning group lists other words for unmeasured claims.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与 antidotal「解毒剂的」混淆；近义组列出其他表示未经测量的说法的词。

normalIntro.en: Anecdotal is an- plus ekdotos: not published, so a private story rather than a public dataset.
normalIntro.cn: anecdotal 就是 an- 加 ekdotos：未公开的，所以是私下的故事，而不是公开的数据集。

normal.en: The fixed phrase is anecdotal evidence, and it is a caution, not praise.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 anecdotal evidence，它是警示而非褒奖。

normal.en: Anecdotally is common in speech: anecdotally, the shop is always full.

normal.en: Do not confuse anecdotal with antidotal, about poisons.

normal.en: The noun is anecdote, stressed on the first syllable.

normal.en: Anecdotal is not the opposite of true; it is the opposite of systematic.
normal.cn: anecdotal 不是「真实」的反面，而是「系统」的反面。

abstract.en: Think of a drawer of unpublished letters.

examples.cn: 这一说法仅依据传闻性证据。

examples.en: Anecdotally, the new timetable has helped.
examples.cn: 据大家反映，新时间表有帮助。

examples.en: The book is anecdotal rather than statistical.
examples.cn: 这本书多轶事而少统计。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one kind of private account: a short entertaining story, and the same story used as weak evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种私下叙述：一段简短有趣的故事，以及同一段故事被当作力度不足的证据。

definition_zh: 贫血；贫血症；（比喻）缺乏活力、萎靡不振
definition_en: a condition in which the blood lacks enough healthy red cells, causing weakness; a lack of vitality
core_image: 脸色苍白、爬两层楼就喘的人：血里少了提气的红细胞
scene: 她最近总是头晕，爬楼梯都费劲。The doctor said her constant fatigue was caused by anemia, so she needed more iron in her diet.
sceneCN: 这里的 anemia 是「贫血症」（第 1 个义项：血液中健康红细胞不足）；句意是医生说她持续的疲劳由贫血引起，需要补铁。

derivatives.zh: 由 anemia 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「贫血的；苍白无力的」

senses.title: A lack of healthy red blood cells
senses.definition: a medical condition in which the blood has too few healthy red cells or too little hemoglobin, causing tiredness and pallor
senses.definitionCN: 血液中健康红细胞或血红蛋白过少的病症，导致疲倦、脸色苍白
senses.example: Heavy periods are a common cause of anemia in young women.
senses.exampleCN: 月经过多是年轻女性贫血的常见原因。
senses.why: The Greek prefix an- means without and haima means blood, so the term literally names a bloodless, blood-poor state.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语前缀 an- 表示「没有」，haima 表示「血」，术语字面就是「缺血、血少」的状态。

senses.title: A lack of vitality or strength
senses.definition: a weakness or lack of vigor in something such as an economy, a team, or a piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 比喻经济、队伍、文章等缺乏生气与力度
senses.example: The report described the anemia of the housing market.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了房地产市场的萎靡不振。
senses.why: A pale, tired patient gave writers a ready image of weak, colorless performance, so the medical word turned figurative.
senses.whyCN: 苍白疲倦的病人给写作者提供了现成的「无力、无血色」意象，医学术语因此转出比喻义。

intro.en: Anemia is a Greek medical compound: an- without plus haima blood.
intro.cn: anemia 是希腊医学复合词：an-（没有）加 haima（血）。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ai- or *sai- referred to vital fluid; its descendants include haima and related blood words.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ai- / *sai- 与生命液体有关，其后续形式包括希腊语 haima 等表示「血」的词。

items.en: Greek haima meant blood, and the compound anaimia named the condition of being without blood, that is, blood-poor.
items.cn: 希腊语 haima 意为「血」，复合词 anaimia 表示「无血、缺血」的状态。

items.en: Medical Latin revived the compound as anaemia when doctors systematized Greek terms.
items.cn: 医生们系统化希腊术语时，医学拉丁语以 anaemia 复兴了这个复合词。

items.en: English anemia is recorded from the early 1800s in medical writing.
items.cn: 英语 anemia 自 19 世纪初见于医学文献。

items.en: By the late 19th century the word had also taken the figurative sense of any lack of vigor.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪后期，该词也发展出「缺乏活力」的比喻义。

note.en: Anemia is often confused with anorexia in form; its adjectives anemic and anaemic differ by spelling system.
note.cn: anemia 易与 anorexia 在字形上混淆；形容词 anemic 与 anaemic 是美式与英式拼法。

entries.definitionCN: 厌食（症），同为 an- 开头的医学词，但词根不同，仅拼写相近

entries.definition: relating to or suffering from anemia; weak and pale

entries.definition: loss of sensation, British spelling

entries.definition: something intensely detested
entries.definitionCN: 令人憎恶之物，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: extreme tiredness
entries.definitionCN: 疲劳，是贫血的主要症状而非病症本身

entries.definition: a lack of energy and enthusiasm
entries.definitionCN: 倦怠；无精打采，与比喻义相近

entries.definition: a state of having no energy or interest
entries.definitionCN: 无精打采，与比喻义相近

entries.definition: the state of being weak
entries.definitionCN: 虚弱；无力，泛指力量不足

entries.definition: an unhealthy pale appearance
entries.definitionCN: 苍白（面色），贫血的典型表征

normalIntro.en: Remember anemia as an- plus haima, without blood.
normalIntro.cn: 把 anemia 记成 an- 加 haima，就是「缺血」。

normal.en: an- means without, seen in anonymous and anarchy.
normal.cn: 前缀 an- 表示「没有」，见于 anonymous、anarchy。

normal.en: haima is the Greek word for blood, kept in hemoglobin.
normal.cn: haima 是希腊语「血」，保留在 hemoglobin（血红蛋白）一词中。

normal.en: So anemia literally means a blood-poor state.
normal.cn: 所以 anemia 字面意思就是「血少」的状态。

normal.en: hematology, the study of blood, shares the same root.
normal.cn: hematology（血液学）用的就是同一个「血」词根。

normal.en: The adjective anemic also means weak or unimpressive.
normal.cn: 形容词 anemic 也表示「软弱无力的、不痛不痒的」。

abstract.en: Picture a pale runner who has to stop halfway up the stairs.
abstract.cn: 想象一个脸色苍白的跑者，爬楼梯爬到一半就停下了。

abstract.en: See a wilting plant that has not been watered for weeks.
abstract.cn: 想象一株几周没浇水的植物，蔫蔫地垂着。

abstract.en: Feel a flat, colorless speech that puts the whole room to sleep.
abstract.cn: 感受一场苍白无力的演讲，让全场昏昏欲睡。

examples.en: She was diagnosed with iron-deficiency anemia last winter.
examples.cn: 去年冬天她被诊断出缺铁性贫血。

examples.en: An anemic performance in the first half cost the team the match.
examples.cn: 上半场软绵绵的表现让球队输掉了比赛。

examples.en: Common symptoms of anemia include dizziness and pale skin.
examples.cn: 贫血的常见症状包括头晕和面色苍白。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from the blood condition to the figurative lack of vigor.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从「血液病症」出发，引申为「缺乏生气的比喻用法」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: blood gone thin, body gone pale and weak
core.cn: 核心意象：血变稀薄，人变得苍白无力

branches.cn: 红细胞过少的医学病症

branches.cn: 从血薄到「气」薄的引申路径

intro.en: Anemia is a transparent Greek compound: negative prefix plus the blood root.
intro.cn: anemia 是透明的希腊语复合词：否定前缀加「血」词根。

latinIntro.en: The haim- family of Greek medical words is large and systematic.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊医学词的 haim- 词族庞大而系统。

definition_zh: n. 心绞痛（心肌缺血引起的胸痛）；咽峡炎
definition_en: Chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle; in older medical use, a severe choking sore throat.
core_image: 胸口被一只看不见的手攥住
scene: 他爬到三楼就得停下，胸口发紧。The doctor diagnosed angina after the stress test.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：爬楼时胸口发紧、休息后缓解，是心肌供血不足引起的心绞痛，医学上称 angina。

senses.title: Chest pain from a short of blood
senses.definition: a squeezing chest pain that appears when the heart muscle does not get enough blood, usually on effort
senses.definitionCN: 心肌供血不足时出现的压榨性胸痛，通常在用力时发作
senses.example: The angina eased once he sat down.
senses.exampleCN: 他一坐下，心绞痛就缓解了。
senses.why: Latin angina meant a choking sore throat, from a root meaning to squeeze; the heart sense keeps the same image of a tightening grip.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 angina 意为「令人窒息的咽痛」，出自意为「挤压」的词根；心脏义保留了同一幅「被攥紧」的画面。

senses.title: The older throat sense
senses.definition: a severe sore throat with swelling that threatens the airway, as in quinsy
senses.definitionCN: 伴肿胀并威胁气道的严重咽痛，如扁桃体周围脓肿
senses.example: The old texts use angina for a strangling throat infection.
senses.exampleCN: 旧文献用 angina 指一种令人窒息的喉部感染。
senses.why: This is the original sense: before cardiology borrowed the word, angina named any condition that felt like being strangled.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：在心脏病学借用该词之前，angina 指任何感觉像被勒住的病症。

intro.en: Angina is Latin for a choking sore throat, from Greek ankhonē, strangling, from ankhein, to squeeze. Heberden added pectoris, of the chest, in 1768 and the modern heart sense was fixed.
intro.cn: angina 在拉丁语中意为「令人窒息的咽痛」，来自希腊语 ankhonē「勒紧」，后者出自 ankhein「挤压」。赫伯登 1768 年加上 pectoris「胸部的」，现代心脏义由此确定。

items.en: Greek ankhonē meant strangling or a strangling, from ankhein, to squeeze tight. The physical image is a hand closing on the throat.
items.cn: 希腊语 ankhonē 意为「勒紧、窒息」，来自 ankhein「紧紧挤压」。身体意象是一只手扣住喉咙。

items.en: Latin angina named a severe sore throat, especially quinsy, and belongs to the same family as angere, to choke, which gives anxious and anger.
items.cn: 拉丁语 angina 指严重咽痛，尤指扁桃体周围脓肿，与 angere「使窒息」同族，后者产生 anxious 与 anger。

items.en: William Heberden described the chest condition in 1768 and called it angina pectoris, angina of the chest, to separate it from the throat disease.
items.cn: 赫伯登 1768 年描述了这种胸部病症，称其为 angina pectoris「胸部绞痛」，以与喉部疾病区分。

items.en: English took angina in the sixteenth century for the throat sense, and the cardiac meaning spread only after Heberden named it.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 angina 指咽喉义，心脏义在赫伯登命名之后才传播开来。

items.en: In current medicine angina alone almost always means the heart condition, and the throat sense survives mainly in older texts.
items.cn: 在当代医学中，单独的 angina 几乎总指心脏病症，咽喉义主要保存在旧文献中。

note.cn: 形近组保留「挤压」词族 angina、anguish、anger、anxious；近义组列出相关病症。

normalIntro.en: Angina shares a root with anger and anguish: all three come from a squeezing grip.
normalIntro.cn: angina 与 anger、anguish 同根：三者都来自「被攥紧」这个动作。

normal.en: Angina pectoris is the full name; pectoris means of the chest.
normal.cn: angina pectoris 是全称，pectoris 意为「胸部的」。

normal.en: It is uncountable: angina, not an angina, though an angina attack is fine.
normal.cn: 它不可数：angina，不说 an angina，但 an angina attack 可以。

normal.en: Stable angina comes on effort; unstable angina comes at rest.
normal.cn: 稳定型心绞痛在用力时发作，不稳定型在静息时发作。

normal.en: Do not confuse angina with anguish, which is suffering in general.
normal.cn: 别把 angina 与 anguish 混淆，后者泛指痛苦。

normal.en: The adjective is anginal, as in anginal pain.
normal.cn: 形容词是 anginal，如 anginal pain。

abstract.en: Picture a fist tightening behind the breastbone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只拳头在胸骨后收紧。

abstract.en: Imagine a staircase that has to be climbed in stages.
abstract.cn: 想象一段必须分几次爬完的楼梯。

abstract.en: Think of a pipe narrowed until the flow slows.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被收窄到水流变慢的管子。

examples.en: He carries tablets for his angina in his coat pocket.
examples.cn: 他外套口袋里装着治心绞痛的药片。

examples.en: The scan showed no sign of angina at rest.
examples.cn: 扫描显示静息时没有心绞痛迹象。

examples.en: Angina pectoris was first described in the eighteenth century.
examples.cn: 心绞痛最早在 18 世纪被描述。

root: 希腊语 ankhein「挤压」生出 ankhonē「勒紧」，拉丁语作 angina 指窒息性咽痛；赫伯登 1768 年加 pectoris「胸部的」，遂指心肌缺血性胸痛。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one grip: the older strangling throat infection, and the modern squeezing pain of a heart short of blood.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一次攥紧：较早的窒息性喉部感染，以及现代心脏缺血时的压榨性疼痛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible hand tightening on the chest
core.cn: 核心意象：一只看不见的手在胸口收紧

branches.en: A tight chest on the third flight of stairs.
branches.cn: 爬到第三层楼梯时发紧的胸口。

branches.en: Pain that fades when the walk stops.
branches.cn: 停下脚步就消退的疼痛。

branches.en: A swollen throat that barely lets air through.
branches.cn: 肿到几乎不通气的喉咙。

branches.en: An old case note naming quinsy.
branches.cn: 一份写着扁桃体脓肿的旧病历。

branches.en: Both feel like being strangled.
branches.cn: 两者都像被勒住。

intro.en: Angina carries the squeeze root ang-, which also builds anger, anxious and anguish.
intro.cn: angina 带着「挤压」词根 ang-，这个词根还构成 anger、anxious 与 anguish。

latinIntro.en: Greek ankhonē became Latin angina; the same Latin angere, to choke, gives anxious and anger, so the family is easy to keep together.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 ankhonē 变成拉丁语 angina；同一个拉丁语 angere「使窒息」产生 anxious 与 anger，所以这个词族很容易一起记。

latinEntries.example: Angina first named the throat disease.

latinEntries.exampleCN: angere 产生 anxious 与 anger。

definition_zh: n. 极度的痛苦；煎熬 v. 使极度痛苦；感到煎熬
definition_en: Severe mental or physical suffering, especially from loss or worry; as a verb, to cause or feel such suffering.
core_image: 心里被拧成一股绳，久久松不开
scene: 她在医院走廊里等了整夜，一句话也说不出。His face showed the anguish of that long wait.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：整夜等待带来的不是普通难过，而是被拧住般的极度煎熬，这就是 anguish。

senses.title: Severe suffering of mind or body
senses.definition: extreme distress caused by loss, fear or pain, beyond ordinary sadness
senses.definitionCN: 由丧失、恐惧或疼痛引起的极度苦恼，超出一般的难过
senses.example: The family waited in anguish for news of the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 那家人在煎熬中等待船的消息。
senses.why: The root means to choke or squeeze, so anguish is distress pictured as a narrowing: the chest tightens and nothing can pass.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「使窒息、挤压」，所以 anguish 是把苦恼想象成「变窄」：胸口收紧，什么都过不去。

senses.title: To suffer or to cause suffering
senses.definition: to feel or inflict severe distress, a literary verbal use
senses.definitionCN: 感到或施加极度苦恼，是较书面的动词用法
senses.example: She anguished over the letter for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 她为那封信煎熬了整整一周。
senses.why: The verb keeps the same squeeze, but now it is something a person does over time rather than a state they are in.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留同一种「拧紧」，只是它变成了一个人持续做的动作，而不是所处的状态。

intro.en: Anguish comes from Latin angustia, distress or narrowness, from angere, to choke. Old French anguisse kept the choking image, and Middle English took it as anguisshe.
intro.cn: anguish 来自拉丁语 angustia「苦恼、狭窄」，出自 angere「使窒息」。古法语 anguisse 保留了「窒息」意象，中古英语借为 anguisshe。

items.en: Latin angere meant to choke, squeeze or strangle. The same root gives angina, anxious, anger and the Latin angustus, narrow.
items.cn: 拉丁语 angere 意为「使窒息、挤压、勒紧」。同一词根产生 angina、anxious、anger 以及拉丁语 angustus「狭窄的」。

items.en: Angustia named tightness and, figuratively, distress: the feeling of being in a narrow place with no room to move.
items.cn: angustia 指「紧窄」，引申为「苦恼」：身处狭窄之地、无处可动的感觉。

items.en: Old French anguisse and angoisse kept the physical sense of a choking sensation in the throat, which is still visible in modern French angoisse.
items.cn: 古法语 anguisse 与 angoisse 保留了「喉部窒息感」的身体义，现代法语 angoisse 中仍可见到。

items.en: Middle English took the word as anguisshe in the thirteenth century, used for both bodily pain and spiritual torment.
items.cn: 中古英语在 13 世纪借为 anguisshe，既指肉体疼痛，也指精神折磨。

items.en: Modern anguish is mostly mental and literary, and the verb use, to anguish over something, is newer and less common.
items.cn: 现代 anguish 多指精神层面且偏书面，动词用法「为某事煎熬」较新且不常见。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against languish, which means to weaken slowly; the near-meaning group lists other words for extreme suffering.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与 languish「渐渐衰弱」混淆；近义组列出其他表示极度痛苦的词。

normalIntro.en: Anguish shares its squeeze root with anger and angina: picture a throat tightening.
normalIntro.cn: anguish 与 anger、angina 共用「挤压」词根：想象喉咙在收紧。

normal.en: The noun is usually uncountable: in anguish, not in an anguish.

normal.en: The verb pattern is anguish over something.

normal.en: Anguished is the common adjective: an anguished cry.

normal.en: Do not confuse anguish with languish, to weaken slowly.

normal.en: Anguish is stronger than distress and more inward than anger.

abstract.cn: 想象一条有人等了整夜的走廊。

abstract.en: Imagine a rope twisted tighter with every hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一根每小时都被拧得更紧的绳。

abstract.en: Think of a letter that cannot be sent or torn up.

examples.en: He anguished over whether to tell the truth.

examples.en: Her anguished face said more than words could.
examples.cn: 她痛苦的表情胜过千言万语。

root: 拉丁语 angere「使窒息」生出 angustia「紧窄、苦恼」，经古法语 anguisse 入中古英语 anguisshe，今作 anguish，字面即「被拧到无处可动的痛苦」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the mind twisted into a rope that will not slacken

branches.en: A night spent waiting for news.

branches.en: A grief too heavy to speak.

branches.en: A week of twisting over one letter.

branches.en: A choice that keeps returning at night.

branches.en: The same squeeze, as state then as act.
branches.cn: 同一次拧紧，先是状态，再是动作。

intro.en: Anguish keeps the squeeze root ang- and the -ish ending, and the same root builds anger, angina and anxious.
intro.cn: anguish 保留「挤压」词根 ang- 与 -ish 词尾，同一词根还构成 anger、angina 与 anxious。

latinIntro.en: Latin angere, to choke, gives angustia, narrowness; Old French anguisse passed it on, and the same root is behind angina.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 angere「使窒息」产生 angustia「狭窄」；古法语 anguisse 把它传下来，同一词根也是 angina 的来源。

items.exampleCN: 令人煎熬的；令人不安的

latinEntries.example: Angere is the root of the family.
Angoisse still means anxiety in French.
latinEntries.exampleCN: angoisse 在法语中仍指焦虑。

definition_zh: n. 动画（制作）；动画片；生气；活力
definition_en: The technique of making still images appear to move, a film made that way, or the quality of being lively and full of spirit.
core_image: 一张张静止的画被喂进一口气，动起来
scene: 这部片子用了三年，每一帧都是手绘的。The animation took three years to finish.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：把逐张手绘的静止画面连续播放，让画面动起来，这门技术与成品都叫 animation。

senses.title: The technique and the film
senses.definition: the method of photographing successive drawings or frames so that they appear to move, and the film produced
senses.definitionCN: 把连续的图画或帧逐一拍摄使其看似运动的方法，以及由此制成的影片
senses.example: The studio released two animations in one year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工作室一年推出了两部动画片。
senses.why: Latin anima means breath or soul, so animation is literally the act of breathing life into something still.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 anima 意为「气息、灵魂」，所以 animation 字面上就是给静止之物吹进一口气的动作。

senses.title: Liveliness of manner
senses.definition: the quality of being energetic and expressive in speech or movement
senses.definitionCN: 言语或动作中精力充沛、富于表现力的特质
senses.example: She told the story with great animation.
senses.exampleCN: 她讲这个故事时眉飞色舞。
senses.why: The same breath is meant, but now in a person: a face or voice that has been given life rather than left flat.
senses.whyCN: 所指的仍是同一口气，只是现在发生在人身上：一张脸或一副嗓音被赋予了生气，而不是平淡无神。

senses.title: The act of giving life
senses.definition: the act of making something live or move, the oldest and most literal sense
senses.definitionCN: 使某物活起来或动起来的行为，是最古老也最字面的义项
senses.example: The animation of the puppet required twelve operators.
senses.exampleCN: 让这具木偶动起来需要十二名操作者。
senses.why: This is the base sense from which both the film technique and the lively manner are extensions.
senses.whyCN: 这是基础义，电影技术与生动神情两个义项都是它的延伸。

intro.en: Animation is Latin animatio, from animare, to give breath to, from anima, breath or soul. The film sense is only about a century old; the older sense is simply life.
intro.cn: animation 来自拉丁语 animatio，出自 animare「赋予气息」，而 animare 又来自 anima「气息、灵魂」。电影义只有约一百年历史；更早的义项就是「生命」。

items.en: Latin anima meant breath, air, and then the soul as the breath of life. The same root gives animal and animate.
items.cn: 拉丁语 anima 意为「气息、空气」，进而指作为生命之息的灵魂。同一词根产生 animal 与 animate。

items.en: Animare meant to fill with breath, to enliven, and also to give a soul to. The verb keeps the physical act of blowing life in.
items.cn: animare 意为「充入气息、使有生气」，也指「赋予灵魂」。这个动词保留了「吹进生命」的身体动作。

items.en: Animatio was the noun of action, an enlivening. It entered English in the sixteenth century for the act of giving life.
items.cn: animatio 是动作名词，意为「赋予生气」。它在 16 世纪进入英语，指赋予生命这一行为。

items.en: The cinematic sense dates from the early twentieth century, when successive drawings were photographed to create movement.
items.cn: 电影义始于 20 世纪初，当时人们把连续的图画逐张拍摄以制造运动感。

items.en: Modern English keeps all three uses: the industry, the lively manner, and the literal giving of life, with animate and animator alongside.
items.cn: 现代英语保留三种用法：产业、生动神情与字面的赋予生命，并配有 animate 与 animator。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the anima family including animus, which means hostility; the near-meaning group lists words for liveliness and cartoons.
note.cn: 形近组保留 anima 词族，包括意为「敌意」的 animus；近义组列出表示活力与卡通的词。

entries.definition: To give life or movement to.
Full of life; made as a cartoon.
entries.definitionCN: 充满生气的；制成动画的。

entries.definition: A person who makes animation.
Hostility or a guiding intention.
The quality of being full of energy.
Strong active energy.
An animated film or a comic drawing.
Lively and animated spirit.

normalIntro.en: Animation is anima plus -tion: breath put into something, whether a drawing or a face.
normalIntro.cn: animation 就是 anima 加 -tion：把气息放进某物，无论那是一张画还是一张脸。

normal.en: Anima means breath, so animation is breathing life in.
normal.cn: anima 意为「气息」，所以 animation 就是吹进生命。

normal.en: Uncountable for the craft, countable for films: two animations.
normal.cn: 指技艺时不可数，指影片时可数：two animations。

normal.en: With animation describes how someone speaks, not what they say.
normal.cn: with animation 描述说话的方式，而不是内容。

normal.en: Do not confuse animus, hostility, with anima, breath.
normal.cn: 别把 animus「敌意」与 anima「气息」混淆。

normal.en: The person is an animator; the adjective is animated.
normal.cn: 从业者是 animator，形容词是 animated。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of drawings flicked into movement.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠画被快速翻动成运动。

abstract.en: Imagine a flat face suddenly lighting up.
abstract.cn: 想象一张平淡的脸忽然亮起来。

abstract.en: Think of a puppet taking its first breath.
abstract.cn: 想象一具木偶吸进第一口气。

examples.en: The animation was drawn entirely by hand.
examples.cn: 这部动画完全由手绘完成。

examples.en: He spoke with an animation that filled the room.
examples.cn: 他讲得眉飞色舞，感染了整个房间。

examples.en: The animation of the model took six months.
examples.cn: 让这个模型动起来花了六个月。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱你妹神」——爱你（ani）妹（ma）神（tion）：给画吹一口「神气」，画就活了，就是动画；人有了这股神气就是活力。

root: 拉丁语 anima「气息、灵魂」生出 animare「赋予气息」，动作名词 animatio 入英语为 animation，本义「赋予生命」，引申为动画技术与生动神情。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses are one breath: life given to a drawing, life showing in a face, and the plain act of giving life.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项是同一口气：吹进画里的生命、显现在脸上的生气，以及「赋予生命」这个本义动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: still drawings fed one breath and starting to move
core.cn: 核心意象：静止的画被喂进一口气后动起来

branches.en: Twelve frames for one second of film.
branches.cn: 一秒影片用十二帧。

branches.en: A studio of hand-drawn features.
branches.cn: 一间手绘长片的工作室。

branches.en: A storyteller with moving hands.
branches.cn: 一个双手不停比划的讲故事者。

branches.en: Twelve operators behind one puppet.
branches.cn: 一具木偶背后的十二名操作者。

branches.en: All three are breath given to something still.
branches.cn: 三者都是把气息给静止之物。

intro.en: Animation is anima plus -ate plus -ion, and the breath root also builds animal, animate and animus.
intro.cn: animation 是 anima 加 -ate 加 -ion，这个「气息」词根还构成 animal、animate 与 animus。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is anima, breath, and animare, to enliven; animatio is the regular noun of action built on that verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 anima「气息」与 animare「使有生气」；animatio 是建立在该动词上的规则动作名词。

latinEntries.example: Anima is the root of the family.
Animatio is the noun of action.

definition_zh: n. 日本动画（日本出品或其风格的动画作品）
definition_en: Animation originating in Japan, or drawn in its distinctive style, often with large eyes and stylised features.
core_image: 大眼睛、尖下巴，一格一格动起来的日本画
scene: 他每周追一集，字幕组当天就更新。Anime has a large following on campus.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：这里指日本出品的动画作品，校园里追看的人很多。anime 在日语里本泛指一切动画。

senses.title: Japanese animation
senses.definition: animation produced in Japan, treated abroad as a distinct medium with its own studios and conventions
senses.definitionCN: 在日本制作的动画，在海外被视为拥有自身工作室与惯例的独立媒介
senses.example: The studio has produced anime for forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工作室制作日本动画已有四十年。
senses.why: In Japanese anime simply means animation of any kind; English narrowed it to the Japanese product when the works began to be exported.
senses.whyCN: 在日语里 anime 泛指任何动画；英语在这些作品开始出口后，把它收窄为「日本出品的动画」。

senses.title: The style, wherever drawn
senses.definition: a visual style with large eyes and stylised features, used even by studios outside Japan
senses.definitionCN: 大眼与风格化五官的视觉风格，连日本以外的工作室也会采用
senses.example: The series is anime in style but made in France.
senses.exampleCN: 这部剧集是日本动画风格，但在法国制作。
senses.why: Once a look becomes recognisable, its name travels with the look rather than the passport of the studio.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某种外观变得可辨识，它的名称就跟着外观走，而不是跟着工作室的国籍走。

intro.en: Anime is a Japanese clipping of animeshon, borrowed from English animation, which goes back to Latin animare. English then borrowed the clipped form back with a narrower meaning.
intro.cn: anime 是日语对 animeshon 的缩略，而 animeshon 借自英语 animation，后者可追溯至拉丁语 animare。英语又把这个缩略形式借回来，含义更窄。

items.en: Latin animare meant to give breath to, from anima, breath. It is the ultimate source of the whole animation family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 animare 意为「赋予气息」，来自 anima「气息」。它是整个 animation 词族的最终来源。

items.en: English animation named the film technique from the early twentieth century, and the word travelled with the exported films.
items.cn: 英语 animation 从 20 世纪初起指这种电影技术，该词随出口影片一同传播。

items.en: Japanese borrowed animation as animeshon, written in katakana, the script used for foreign loanwords.
items.cn: 日语把 animation 借为 animeshon，用片假名书写，那是用于外来语的字体。

items.en: Japanese shortened animeshon to anime in the 1970s, and in Japan the word covers all animation, domestic or foreign.
items.cn: 日语在 20 世纪 70 年代把 animeshon 缩略为 anime，在日本该词涵盖一切动画，无论国产或外国。

items.en: English took anime back in the 1980s for Japanese work only, a narrower sense than the Japanese original.
items.cn: 英语在 20 世纪 80 年代把 anime 借回，专指日本作品，比日语原义更窄。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the anim- family and the sociological term anomie; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring Japanese and cartoon forms.
note.cn: 形近组保留 anim- 词族与社会学术语 anomie；近义组列出相邻的日本与卡通形式。

entries.definition: The technique of making images move.
To give life or movement to.
A breakdown of social norms.
A living creature that moves and feeds.
Japanese comic books and graphic novels.
An animated film or comic drawing.
A cartoon, in casual speech.

normalIntro.en: Anime is animation clipped in Japanese and borrowed back, so it is the same word with a passport stamp.
normalIntro.cn: anime 是 animation 在日语中被缩略后又借回英语，所以是同一个词多盖了一个出入境章。

normal.en: In Japan anime means all animation; in English it means Japanese animation.
normal.cn: 在日本 anime 指一切动画，在英语中指日本动画。

normal.en: It is usually uncountable: watch anime, not watch an anime, unless you mean one series.
normal.cn: 通常不可数：watch anime；除非指某一部剧集，才说 an anime。

normal.en: Pronounce it with three syllables, not like the English word anime.
normal.cn: 读作三个音节，不要按英语拼读习惯读成两音节。

normal.en: Manga is printed comics; anime is the moving form.
normal.cn: manga 是纸质漫画，anime 是会动的那种。

normal.en: Do not confuse anime with anomie, a sociology term.
normal.cn: 别把 anime 与 anomie「社会失范」混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a word travelling out and coming back shorter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词出国一趟，回来时变短了。

abstract.en: Imagine large eyes blinking on a hand-drawn face.
abstract.cn: 想象一张手绘脸上大眼睛在眨动。

abstract.en: Think of a style that keeps its name after crossing a border.
abstract.cn: 想象一种风格过了国境仍保留自己的名字。

examples.en: The festival screens classic anime from the 1980s.
examples.cn: 影展放映 20 世纪 80 年代的经典日本动画。

examples.en: She draws in anime style but writes her own scripts.
examples.cn: 她用日本动画风格作画，但剧本自己写。

examples.en: Anime conventions now attract fans from many countries.
examples.cn: 日本动画展会如今吸引多国粉丝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿尼妹」——阿尼（ani）妹（me）：日本动画里那些大眼睛的妹妹角色，就是 anime；比 animation 少了尾巴，是日语缩略。

root: 拉丁语 animare「赋予气息」经英语 animation 借入日语作 animeshon，20 世纪 70 年代缩略为 anime 泛指动画；英语 80 年代借回，专指日本动画及其风格。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one imported look: the Japanese product itself, and the same visual style used anywhere.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种舶来外观：日本出品的作品本身，以及在任何地方使用的同一视觉风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: big-eyed Japanese drawings moving frame by frame
core.cn: 核心意象：大眼睛的日本画一格一格动起来

branches.en: A Tokyo studio with forty years of work.
branches.cn: 一间有四十年作品的东京工作室。

branches.en: A weekly series with same-day subtitles.
branches.cn: 一部当天就有字幕的周更剧集。

branches.en: A French series drawn with large eyes.
branches.cn: 一部画着大眼睛的法国剧集。

branches.en: A style copied by studios worldwide.
branches.cn: 一种被各地工作室模仿的风格。

branches.en: One look, first a place then a style.
branches.cn: 同一种外观，先指产地，再指风格。

intro.en: Anime carries the anim- breath root through English animation, and sits beside manga in the same loanword family.
intro.cn: anime 经英语 animation 带着 anim-「气息」词根，并与 manga 同属一个外来词家族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is animare, reached through English animation and Japanese animeshon; the clipping itself happened in Japanese.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 animare，经英语 animation 与日语 animeshon 抵达；缩略这一步发生在日语中。

definition_zh: n. 注释；批注；（数据或基因的）标注
definition_en: A note added to a text, image or dataset to explain or comment on it; in biology, the labelling of features in a genome sequence.
core_image: 在正文旁边空白处写下的一行小字
scene: 他在页边写满了自己的疑问和补充。Every annotation in the margin is in his own hand.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：页边空白处那些解释与评论的小字就是 annotation，是加在原文之外的注记。

senses.title: A note added to a text
senses.definition: an explanatory or critical note written beside or below a passage
senses.definitionCN: 写在一段文字旁边或下方的解释性或评论性注记
senses.example: The edition carries annotations on every page.
senses.exampleCN: 这个版本每一页都有注释。
senses.why: Latin annotare meant to mark beside, from ad-, to, and nota, a mark; the note is literally placed next to the text rather than inside it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 annotare 意为「在旁边做标记」，由 ad-「向」与 nota「标记」构成；注记字面上是放在文本旁边，而不是文本里面。

senses.title: Labelling in data and genomes
senses.titleCN: 数据与基因组中的标注
senses.definition: the tagging of features in a dataset or sequence so that a machine or reader can use them
senses.definitionCN: 为数据集或序列中的特征打标签，使机器或读者能够使用
senses.example: Genome annotation identifies where each gene begins.
senses.exampleCN: 基因组注释标出每个基因的起始位置。
senses.why: The same act of marking beside is now done at scale: the sequence is the text, and the labels are the marginal notes.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「在旁边标记」的动作如今大规模进行：序列就是正文，标签就是页边注。

intro.en: Annotation is Latin annotatio, from annotare, to mark beside, from ad-, to, and nota, a mark. The word keeps the picture of a note written in the margin.
intro.cn: annotation 来自拉丁语 annotatio，出自 annotare「在旁边做标记」，由 ad-「向」与 nota「标记」构成。这个词保留了「在页边写注」的画面。

items.en: Latin ad- meant to or toward, and assimilates to an- before n, which is why the word has a double n.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 意为「向、朝」，在 n 前同化为 an-，这就是该词有双写 n 的原因。

items.en: Latin nota meant a mark, sign or letter, and gives note, notation, notable and denote.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nota 意为「标记、符号、字母」，产生 note、notation、notable 与 denote。

items.en: Annotare meant to mark beside or add a note to, the working verb of scholars reading with a pen in hand.
items.cn: annotare 意为「在旁边标记、加注」，是学者手执笔阅读时的常用动词。

items.en: Annotatio was the noun of action, and English took annotation in the sixteenth century for the note itself as well as the act.
items.cn: annotatio 是动作名词，英语在 16 世纪借入 annotation，既指注记本身，也指加注这一行为。

items.en: Modern English extends annotation to code, images and genome sequences, and the verb annotate is now common in data work.
items.cn: 现代英语把 annotation 扩展到代码、图像与基因组序列，动词 annotate 在数据工作中已很常见。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the nota family and contrasts denotation; the near-meaning group lists other words for an added note.
note.cn: 形近组保留 nota 词族并与 denotation 对照；近义组列出其他表示附加注记的词。

entries.definition: To add notes to a text.
A person who adds notes.
Provided with notes.
The literal meaning of a word.
A short written comment.
A brief explanation of a difficult word.
A sustained set of explanations.
A note printed at the bottom of a page.

normalIntro.en: Annotation is ad- plus nota plus -tion: a mark placed beside the text.
normalIntro.cn: annotation 就是 ad- 加 nota 加 -tion：放在文本旁边的一个标记。

normal.en: The verb is annotate, the person an annotator.
normal.cn: 动词是 annotate，人是 annotator。

normal.en: It is countable: an annotation, several annotations.
normal.cn: 它可数：an annotation、several annotations。

normal.en: An annotated edition is one with notes added.
normal.cn: annotated edition 指加了注释的版本。

normal.en: Do not confuse annotation with denotation, literal meaning.
normal.cn: 别把 annotation 与 denotation「字面意义」混淆。

normal.en: Genome annotation is the standard term in biology.
normal.cn: genome annotation 是生物学中的标准术语。

abstract.en: Picture a margin crowded with small handwriting.
abstract.cn: 想象页边挤满了细小的手写字。

abstract.en: Imagine a sequence with coloured labels above each gene.
abstract.cn: 想象一段序列，每个基因上方都有彩色标签。

abstract.en: Think of a reader talking back to the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个读者对着书页回话。

examples.en: Each annotation explains a difficult allusion.
examples.cn: 每条注释解释一处难懂的典故。

examples.en: The team spent a year on genome annotation.
examples.cn: 团队花了一年做基因组注释。

examples.en: He annotated the manuscript in red ink.
examples.cn: 他用红墨水给手稿加注。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：an「向」+ not「标记」+ ation「动作」——朝着正文旁边做标记，就是注释、批注。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」在 n 前同化为 an-，加 nota「标记」构成 annotare「在旁边标记」，动作名词 annotatio 入英语为 annotation，字面即「加在旁边的注记」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one mark placed beside: a scholar note in a margin, and a label attached to data or a sequence.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个放在旁边的标记：学者写在页边的注，以及贴在数据或序列上的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of small writing in the margin beside the text
core.cn: 核心意象：正文旁边空白处的一行小字

branches.en: A page of notes in a student hand.
branches.cn: 一页学生笔迹的注记。

branches.en: A footnote explaining an allusion.
branches.cn: 一条解释典故的脚注。

branches.en: Labels marking each gene start.
branches.cn: 标出每个基因起点的标签。

branches.en: Boxes drawn around objects in images.
branches.cn: 在图像中物体周围画的框。

branches.en: Both add a mark beside the original.
branches.cn: 两者都在原件旁边加标记。

intro.en: Annotation is ad- plus nota plus -ation, and the nota root builds note, notation, denote and notable.
intro.cn: annotation 是 ad- 加 nota 加 -ation，nota 词根还构成 note、notation、denote 与 notable。

definition_zh: 宣布；通告；播报；预示
definition_en: to make something known officially and publicly, to read it out aloud, or to be a sign that something is coming
core_image: 麦克风前一张嘴向人群送出消息
scene: 会议室的门打开，负责人走上台，手里拿着一页纸。The company announced a new product on Monday.
sceneCN: 这里 announce 是「宣布」（第 1 个义项：正式公开告知）；句意是公司在周一宣布了一款新产品。

pos.zh: 动词：宣布；通告；播报；预示

derivatives.zh: 名词：宣告，特指天使报喜

senses.title: To make known publicly
senses.definition: to tell people about a plan, decision, or fact in an official and public way
senses.definitionCN: 以正式、公开的方式把计划、决定或事实告诉众人
senses.example: The company announced a new product on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在周一宣布了一款新产品。
senses.why: The Latin verb means 'to bring news to', so the act is one of carrying a message from those who know to those who do not.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁语动词意为「把消息带给」，因此这一动作就是把消息从知情者送到不知情者那里。

senses.title: To read out as a broadcaster
senses.definition: to read out names, times, or news aloud, as a broadcaster or official does
senses.definitionCN: 像播音员或工作人员那样，出声报出姓名、时间或消息
senses.example: The announcer announced the departure of the last train.
senses.exampleCN: 播音员播报了末班车的发车信息。
senses.why: Broadcasting turned the public statement into a spoken routine, so the same verb covers reading out a train time.
senses.whyCN: 广播把公开声明变成一种口头例行工作，于是同一个动词也用来报出列车时刻。

senses.title: To be a sign of
senses.definition: to make something clear by being a visible sign that it is coming
senses.definitionCN: 以可见的迹象说明某事即将到来
senses.example: The first buds announced the return of spring.
senses.exampleCN: 初生的嫩芽预示春天回来了。
senses.why: If news arrives before an event, then anything that arrives before an event can announce it, even a bud.
senses.whyCN: 如果消息先于事件到达，那么任何先于事件出现的东西都能 announce 它，哪怕只是一枚嫩芽。

intro.en: Announce carries the Latin word for a messenger inside it.
intro.cn: announce 里面藏着拉丁语表示「信使」的那个词。

items.en: nuntius meant 'messenger' and also 'message'.
items.cn: nuntius 既指「信使」，也指「消息」。

items.en: annuntiare meant 'to bring news to', built with ad- 'to'.
items.cn: annuntiare 意为「把消息带给」，由 ad-「向」构成。

items.en: French anoncer carried the word into English.
items.cn: 法语 anoncer 把这个词带入英语。

items.en: English announce first meant to proclaim something officially.
items.cn: 英语 announce 最初意为正式宣告某事。

items.en: Broadcasting added the sense of reading out names and times.
items.cn: 广播业增添了报出姓名与时间的义项。

items.en: The 'be a sign of' sense grows from news arriving before an event.
items.cn: 「预示」义来自消息先于事件到达这一想法。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the same messenger root; the near-meaning group differs in how public or forceful the statement is.
note.cn: 形近组共享「信使」词根；近义组按公开程度与语气强弱区分。

items.meaning: a person who reads out news

definition_zh: 使恼火；惹烦；（旧）骚扰、袭扰
definition_en: to make someone feel slightly angry, or, in older military use, to harass a place or force repeatedly
core_image: 一只关不掉、一直滴水的水龙头
scene: 楼上的音乐一遍遍重复同一段旋律，楼下的人合上了书。The constant noise from the flat above annoyed her.
sceneCN: 这里 annoy 是「使恼火」（第 1 个义项：让人心里生出轻微怒气）；句意是楼上不断的噪声让她恼火。

senses.title: To make someone slightly angry
senses.definition: to make a person feel slightly angry or irritated, usually by something repeated or small
senses.definitionCN: 使人心里生出轻微的怒气或不快，通常由反复出现的小事引起
senses.example: The constant noise from the flat above annoyed her.
senses.exampleCN: 楼上不断的噪声让她很恼火。
senses.why: The old French verb meant 'to trouble and weary', a weariness that the modern everyday sense keeps.
senses.whyCN: 这个古法语动词意为「使困扰、使厌倦」，现代日常义里仍保留着这种被磨出来的疲惫感。

senses.title: To harass, in older military use
senses.definition: to attack or trouble an enemy or a place repeatedly without a full battle
senses.definitionCN: 不进行正式会战，而反复袭扰敌人或某地
senses.example: Enemy patrols annoyed the column all night.
senses.exampleCN: 敌方巡逻队整夜袭扰这支行军纵队。
senses.why: The earliest English sense was to harm or molest, and military writing kept that harder meaning after everyday speech softened it.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的义项是伤害或侵扰，日常口语把词义软化之后，军事文本仍保留了这层更硬的意味。

intro.en: Annoy began with hatred, then softened into everyday irritation.
intro.cn: annoy 最初与憎恨有关，后来才软化为日常的烦躁。

items.en: odium meant 'hatred', the emotional core of the family.
items.cn: odium 意为「憎恨」，是这个词族的情感核心。

items.en: inodiare meant 'to make hateful', built with in- on odium.
items.cn: inodiare 意为「使可憎」，由 in- 加 odium 构成。

items.en: anuier meant 'to trouble, molest, weary'.
items.cn: anuier 意为「使困扰、侵扰、使厌倦」。

items.en: English annoy first meant to harm or molest.
items.cn: 英语 annoy 最初意为伤害或侵扰。

items.en: Everyday use keeps the milder sense; the military sense survives in older writing.
items.cn: 日常用法保留较温和的义项，军事义多见于较早的文本。

note.en: The look-alike group is the annoy family; the near-meaning group grades how strong or how repeated the irritation is.
note.cn: 形近组是 annoy 词族；近义组按恼人程度与反复程度分级。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is odium, 'hatred', still visible behind the French shape of the word.

items.meaning: the feeling or cause of being annoyed

definition_zh: n. 烦恼；恼怒；令人厌烦的人或事
definition_en: The feeling of being mildly angry or irritated, or a person or thing that causes that feeling.
core_image: 一只在耳边绕圈的蚊子，赶不走
scene: 楼上装修的电钻声从早响到晚。The noise from upstairs is a constant annoyance.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：这里不是指情绪，而是指「引起烦扰的东西」——楼上不断的电钻声本身就是一件烦扰。

forms.label: 复数（指具体烦扰事物时）

senses.title: The feeling of irritation
senses.definition: a mild anger caused by something troublesome or repeatedly disturbing
senses.definitionCN: 由麻烦或反复干扰之事引起的轻度怒气
senses.example: She could not hide her annoyance at the interruption.
senses.exampleCN: 她无法掩饰被打断时的恼火。
senses.why: The word descends from a Latin phrase meaning it is hateful to me, so the feeling is literally something made hateful to you.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自一句意为「它令我憎恶」的拉丁语短语，所以这种情绪字面上就是「被弄成令你憎恶的东西」。

senses.title: The thing that irritates
senses.definition: a person, noise or habit that produces that feeling
senses.definitionCN: 产生这种感觉的人、噪声或习惯
senses.example: The dripping tap became a real annoyance.
senses.exampleCN: 那个滴水的水龙头成了真正的烦扰。
senses.why: English often turns a feeling noun into the name of its cause, and annoyance is a standard example: the noise is an annoyance.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把情绪名词转用为其原因的名称，annoyance 是典型例子：那噪声本身就是一件烦扰。

intro.en: Annoyance is built on annoy, which comes from Old French anui, from Late Latin inodiare, to make hateful, from the Latin phrase mihi in odio est, it is hateful to me.
intro.cn: annoyance 建立在 annoy 之上，annoy 来自古法语 anui，后者出自晚期拉丁语 inodiare「使可憎」，源于拉丁语短语 mihi in odio est「它令我憎恶」。

items.en: Latin odium meant hatred, and the phrase mihi in odio est meant it is hateful to me. The same root gives odious.
items.cn: 拉丁语 odium 意为「憎恨」，短语 mihi in odio est 意为「它令我憎恶」。同一词根产生 odious。

items.en: Late Latin inodiare turned that phrase into a verb meaning to make hateful, to trouble or offend.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 inodiare 把那句短语变成动词，意为「使可憎、使烦扰、冒犯」。

items.en: Old French anui and the verb anuier kept the sense of trouble, distress and irritation, and passed it to English.
items.cn: 古法语 anui 及动词 anuier 保留「烦扰、苦恼、恼怒」之义，并传入英语。

items.en: Middle English took the verb as anoyen in the thirteenth century, originally for serious harm as well as minor irritation.
items.cn: 中古英语在 13 世纪借为动词 anoyen，最初既指严重伤害，也指轻微烦扰。

items.en: Annoyance is formed with -ance, and English weakened the sense from harm to everyday irritation, then extended it to the cause.
items.cn: annoyance 用 -ance 构成，英语把含义从「伤害」弱化为日常「恼火」，再扩展到指引起恼火的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against noisome, which means foul-smelling, not noisy; the near-meaning group lists other words for irritation.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与 noisome 混淆，它意为「恶臭的」而非「吵闹的」；近义组列出其他表示恼火的词。

normal.en: Uncountable for the feeling, countable for causes: an annoyance.

definition_en: a fixed sum of money paid each year, or the contract providing it
core_image: 每年准时寄到的一笔钱：像一棵按时结果的树
scene: 退休教师打开信封，里面又是那笔固定的款项。The retired teacher lives on an annuity from her late husband's pension fund.
sceneCN: 这里 annuity 是「年金」（第 1 个义项：按年支付的固定款项）；句意为：退休教师靠亡夫养老基金支付的年金生活。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁短语借入，义为「每年」

senses.title: A yearly payment of money
senses.definition: a fixed sum paid once a year to a person
senses.definitionCN: 每年一次付给某人的固定款项
senses.example: The trust pays her an annuity of ten thousand dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 信托每年付给她一万美元年金。
senses.why: The Latin annus means year, so the word names a payment defined by the year.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 annus 意为「年」，该词即指以「年」为单位的支付。

senses.title: The contract or investment providing such payment
senses.definition: a financial contract that guarantees periodic payments, usually in retirement
senses.definitionCN: 保证定期给付的金融契约，多用于退休
senses.example: He converted his savings into a life annuity.
senses.exampleCN: 他把积蓄转换成了终身年金。
senses.why: The payment and the legal machine behind it share one name.
senses.whyCN: 支付行为与背后的法律装置共用一个名称。

senses.title: Payments more frequent than yearly
senses.definition: a series of equal periodic payments, even monthly or quarterly
senses.definitionCN: 等额的定期给付序列，即便按月或按季
senses.example: Most annuities now pay monthly rather than annually.
senses.exampleCN: 如今多数年金按月而非按年给付。
senses.why: The yearly frame stretched to fit any equal interval.
senses.whyCN: 「按年」的框架被拉伸以适配任何等距时段。

senses.title: A life annuity: income until death
senses.definition: an annuity that pays until the holder's death
senses.definitionCN: 支付至持有人去世为止的年金
senses.example: A life annuity removes the fear of outliving savings.
senses.exampleCN: 终身年金消除了「人还在、钱没了」的恐惧。
senses.why: The insurance pool trades a lump sum for a promise without an end date.
senses.whyCN: 保险池以一笔一次性款项换取一份没有截止日的承诺。

senses.title: A deferred annuity: payment that starts later
senses.definition: an annuity whose payments begin at a chosen future date
senses.definitionCN: 在选定的未来日期才开始给付的年金
senses.example: Her deferred annuity starts when she turns sixty-five.
senses.exampleCN: 她的递延年金在她六十五岁时开始给付。
senses.why: The promise can sleep for years before it starts paying.
senses.whyCN: 承诺可以先沉睡多年再开始兑现。

senses.title: An annuity in feudal history
senses.definition: a yearly grant of money from a lord, crown, or institution
senses.definitionCN: 领主、王室或机构授予的年度钱款
senses.example: The poet received a royal annuity in 1619.
senses.exampleCN: 这位诗人于 1619 年获得王室年俸。
senses.why: Before insurance, the crown itself was the payer of yearly sums.
senses.whyCN: 在保险出现之前，王室本身就是年款的支付者。

senses.title: Annuity as steady, reliable income
senses.definition: any reliable source of regular income, likened to an annuity
senses.definitionCN: 被比作年金的任何稳定定期收入
senses.example: The hit song became an annuity for its writer.
senses.exampleCN: 那首热门歌曲成了词作者的稳定财源。
senses.why: What pays regularly without further work feels like an annuity.
senses.whyCN: 无需再劳作仍定期入账之物，感觉便如年金。

senses.title: Annuity certain: payments for a fixed term
senses.definition: an annuity that pays for a set number of years, however long the holder lives
senses.definitionCN: 不论持有人寿命长短、给付固定年数的年金
senses.example: He chose an annuity certain for fifteen years.
senses.exampleCN: 他选择了为期十五年的定期年金。
senses.why: The promise can be bounded by years instead of by a lifespan.
senses.whyCN: 承诺的边界可以是「年数」而非「寿命」。

intro.en: Annuity is the Latin year turned into money: a payment that the calendar itself calls for.
intro.cn: annuity 是被金钱化的拉丁「年」：一笔由历法本身召唤的支付。

items.en: The root *at- meant to go, and the completed circuit became the year.
items.cn: 印欧词根 *at- 意为「行走」，走完一圈即为「年」，一般认为如此。

items.en: Annus meant year; the adjective annualis meant yearly.
items.cn: 拉丁语 annus 意为「年」，形容词 annualis 意为「每年的」。

items.en: Annuitas named a yearly payment or obligation in legal documents.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 annuitas 在法律文书中指年付钱款或义务。

items.en: Old French carried annuite into the language of law and finance.
items.cn: 古法语 annuite 进入法律与金融语言。

items.en: English adopted annuity in the fifteenth century, first for royal yearly grants, later for insurance contracts.
items.cn: 英语于十五世纪借入 annuity，最初指王室年赐，后指保险契约。

note.en: Grouped by the shared year-root and by neighboring financial words.
note.cn: 按共享「年」词根与金融近义词分组。

entries.definition: occurring once a year
entries.definitionCN: 每年的，与 annuity 同出 annus 词根

entries.definition: year-by-year historical records
entries.definitionCN: 编年史，同根且同样按年组织

entries.definition: conversion of figures to a yearly rate
entries.definitionCN: 年化计算，同根且同为金融用语

entries.definition: regular payment after retirement
entries.definitionCN: 养老金，与年金常互换但来源多为职业计划

entries.definition: a fixed regular payment, as to a scholar
entries.definitionCN: 津贴；薪俸，多为职业性定期支付

entries.definition: a regular sum provided for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 定期给予的款项，多指生活或专项津贴

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real annus root and the standard financial family.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于真实的 annus 词根及标准金融词族。

normal.en: annus = year; an annuity is money that arrives by the year.
normal.cn: annus 表「年」；annuity 即「按年而来的钱」。

normal.en: Same family: annual, anniversary, per annum, biennial.
normal.cn: 同族词：annual、anniversary、per annum、biennial。

normal.en: The annuitant is the person who receives the annuity.
normal.cn: annuitant 是领取年金的人。

normal.en: A life annuity pays until death; a deferred annuity starts later.
normal.cn: 终身年金付至身故；递延年金晚些开始给付。

normal.en: Annals record by year; annuities pay by year: same root, two directions.
normal.cn: annals 按年记录，annuity 按年支付：同根两向。

abstract.en: Picture a tree that drops the same number of coins into your yard every spring.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵每年春天往你院子里落下等量硬币的树。

abstract.en: See a calendar page turning, and with each turn a coin lands in a bowl.
abstract.cn: 想象日历每翻一页，一枚硬币落进碗里。

abstract.en: Feel the calm of a bill you never have to earn again.
abstract.cn: 感受一笔不必再去挣的钱带来的安心。

examples.en: She bought an annuity to secure her retirement income.
examples.cn: 她购买了年金以保障退休收入。

examples.en: The fellowship carries a generous annuity.
examples.cn: 该研究基金附带丰厚的年俸。

examples.en: Royalties from the textbook are his private annuity.
examples.cn: 教科书的版税是他私人的稳定财源。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「按年贴」——按年给付、贴补生活的钱，正是 annuity（年金）。

root: 拉丁语 annus（年，源自一般认为的印欧词根 *at-「行走」，走完一循环为一年）→ 中世纪拉丁语 annuitas「年付钱款」→ 古法语 annuite → 英语 annuity（15 世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: From the yearly payment, the word grows into contracts, insurance products, royal grants, and any metaphorical stream of steady money.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「年付之款」出发，词义生长为契约、保险产品、王室年赐，以及任何比喻性的稳定财源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same sum landing every year, like fruit in season
core.cn: 核心意象：每年准时落下的等额之款，如应季果实

branches.en: the payment itself, by year or by month
branches.cn: 给付本身，按年或按月

branches.en: the contracts that guarantee payment
branches.cn: 担保给付的各类契约

branches.en: historical grants from crown or lord
branches.cn: 历史上的王室或领主年赐

branches.en: steady income in metaphor
branches.cn: 比喻中的稳定收入

branches.en: money that outlives the work
branches.cn: 超越劳作本身的钱财

intro.en: Annuity belongs to the compact ann- year family, all members counting time in years.
intro.cn: annuity 属于紧凑的 ann-「年」词族，所有成员都以「年」计时间。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin combined annus with the noun suffix -itas to name the yearly obligation.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语以 annus 加名词后缀 -itas 构成年付义务之名。

items.example: Per annum means for each year.
Civility and utility share this ending.
items.exampleCN: civility 与 utility 共用此词尾。

items.example: The annuitant cashed the yearly cheque.
items.exampleCN: 受益人兑现了年度支票。
他们庆祝了金婚纪念日。
两年一度的报告追踪进展。

definition_zh: v. 宣告（婚姻、合同等）无效；废除；取消
definition_en: To declare a marriage, contract or official act legally void, as if it had never existed.
core_image: 把那份文件从头到尾划掉，当作没发生过
scene: 法院认定这段婚姻自始就不成立。The court agreed to annul the marriage.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：annul 不是「离婚」，而是宣告这段婚姻自始无效，法律上当作从未存在。

forms.label: 过去式与过去分词（双写 l）

senses.title: To declare legally void
senses.definition: to rule that a marriage or contract never had legal force, so it is treated as never having existed
senses.definitionCN: 裁定某段婚姻或合同从未具有法律效力，因而视为从未存在
senses.example: They sought to annul the marriage on grounds of fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以欺诈为由申请宣告婚姻无效。
senses.why: Latin nullus means not any, so annul literally makes a thing into nothing: the record is not ended but erased from the start.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nullus 意为「没有任何一个」，所以 annul 字面上是把某物变成「无」：记录不是被终止，而是从头被抹去。

senses.title: To cancel or abolish generally
senses.titleCN: 一般意义上的取消或废除
senses.definition: to cancel an act, result or arrangement so that it no longer counts
senses.definitionCN: 取消某项行为、结果或安排，使其不再生效
senses.example: The board voted to annul the earlier resolution.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会投票撤销先前的决议。
senses.why: Outside strict law the word keeps the same zeroing image, but the erasure is practical rather than retroactive.
senses.whyCN: 在严格法律之外，该词保留同一幅「归零」画面，只是抹除是实际层面的，而非追溯性的。

intro.en: Annul is Late Latin annullare, from ad-, to, and nullus, not any, from ne-, not, and ullus, any. The word literally means to reduce to nothing.
intro.cn: annul 来自晚期拉丁语 annullare，由 ad-「向」与 nullus「没有任何一个」构成，而 nullus 又由 ne-「不」与 ullus「任何」组成。这个词字面意为「使归于无」。

items.en: Latin nullus meant not any, built from ne-, not, and ullus, any. It gives null, nullify, nullity and annihilate.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nullus 意为「没有任何一个」，由 ne-「不」与 ullus「任何」构成。它产生 null、nullify、nullity 与 annihilate。

items.en: The prefix ad- assimilates to an- before n, which produces the double n and distinguishes annul from annual.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 在 n 前同化为 an-，形成双写 n，也把 annul 与 annual 区分开。

items.en: Annullare meant to reduce to nothing, and was used in church law for declaring a marriage void from the beginning.
items.cn: annullare 意为「使归于无」，在教会法中用于宣告婚姻自始无效。

items.en: Old French annuller passed the verb into Middle English in the fifteenth century, keeping the legal sense.
items.cn: 古法语 annuller 在 15 世纪把该动词传入中古英语，保留法律义。

items.en: Modern English doubles the l before -ed and -ing, and the noun annulment is the standard term in family law.
items.cn: 现代英语在 -ed 与 -ing 前双写 l，名词 annulment 是家事法中的标准术语。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against annual, about years; the near-meaning group lists other words for cancelling legal force.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与 annual「每年的」混淆；近义组列出其他表示取消法律效力的词。

entries.definition: The act of declaring void.
Having no legal force; zero.
To make legally void or ineffective.
Happening once a year.
To call off something planned.
To withdraw a licence or order.
To make legally invalid.
To cancel a contract or rule.

normalIntro.en: Annul is an- plus null: reduce to nothing, so the act is treated as never having happened.
normalIntro.cn: annul 就是 an- 加 null：使归于无，所以那件事被当作从未发生。

normal.en: Double the l: annulled, annulling, but annuls.
normal.cn: 双写 l：annulled、annulling，但 annuls。

normal.en: Annulment erases from the start; divorce ends a valid marriage.
normal.cn: annulment 从头抹去，divorce 结束一段有效婚姻。

normal.en: Do not confuse annul with annual, about years.
normal.cn: 别把 annul 与 annual「每年的」混淆。

normal.en: The noun is annulment, not annulation.
normal.cn: 名词是 annulment，不是 annulation。

normal.en: Null and void is the fixed legal pair.
normal.cn: null and void 是固定法律搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a document crossed out from the first line to the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文件从第一行到最后一行被划掉。

abstract.en: Imagine a record that is removed rather than closed.
abstract.cn: 想象一份被移除而非被封存的记录。

abstract.en: Think of a number reset to zero instead of counted down.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被重置为零而非倒数的数字。

examples.en: The court will annul the contract if fraud is proved.
examples.cn: 若证实欺诈，法院将宣告合同无效。

examples.en: They applied to annul the marriage after two months.
examples.cn: 两个月后他们申请宣告婚姻无效。

examples.en: The committee annulled the result and ordered a recount.
examples.cn: 委员会宣布结果无效并下令重新计票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：an「向」+ nul「零、无」——把一份文件推向「零」，当作从未存在，就是宣告无效 annul。

root: 拉丁语 ne-「不」+ ullus「任何」构成 nullus「没有任何一个」，加 ad- 成 annullare「使归于无」，经古法语 annuller 入英语为 annul，指宣告自始无效。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one zeroing: the strict legal erasure of a marriage or contract, and the everyday cancelling of a decision.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一次归零：严格法律上对婚姻或合同的抹除，以及日常对一项决定的取消。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a document struck through as if it never existed
core.cn: 核心意象：一份被划掉、当作从未存在的文件

branches.en: A marriage erased from the register.
branches.cn: 一段从登记册上抹去的婚姻。

branches.en: A contract void from the first day.
branches.cn: 一份自第一天起就无效的合同。

branches.en: A resolution struck from the minutes.
branches.cn: 一项从会议记录中删去的决议。

branches.en: An election result set aside.
branches.cn: 一个被搁置的选举结果。

branches.en: Both turn something into nothing.
branches.cn: 两者都把某物变成无。

intro.en: Annul is ad- plus null, and the null root builds nullify, nullity and annihilate.
intro.cn: annul 是 ad- 加 null，null 词根还构成 nullify、nullity 与 annihilate。

latinIntro.en: Latin nullus is ne-, not, plus ullus, any; adding ad- gives annullare, to reduce to nothing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nullus 由 ne-「不」加 ullus「任何」构成；加上 ad- 得到 annullare「使归于无」。

latinEntries.exampleCN: nullus 产生 null 与 annul。

latinEntries.example: Ullus is the second half of nullus.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ullus 是 nullus 的后半部分。

definition_zh: n. 按蚊；疟蚊（传播疟疾的蚊属）
definition_en: A mosquito of the genus Anopheles, the only group that transmits human malaria, resting with its body tilted upward.
core_image: 停在浅水边、身子翘起来的那只细腿蚊子
scene: 村里排干了那片水洼，蚊子少了一大半。An anopheles was found in the drained puddle.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：在那片浅水洼里发现的蚊子属于按蚊属，也就是能传播疟疾的那一类，学名 Anopheles。

senses.title: The mosquito genus
senses.definition: a mosquito of the genus Anopheles, recognisable by its raised resting posture and spotted wings
senses.definitionCN: 按蚊属的蚊子，以停息时身体上翘的姿态与带斑的翅为特征
senses.example: The anopheles rests with its abdomen pointing up.
senses.exampleCN: 按蚊停息时腹部朝上翘起。
senses.why: Greek anopheles meant useless or harmful, from an-, not, and ophelos, benefit; the name was a judgement on the insect, not a description.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 anopheles 意为「无用的、有害的」，由 an-「不」与 ophelos「益处」构成；这个名字是对该昆虫的评价，而不是描述。

senses.title: The malaria vector
senses.definition: the insect considered as the carrier of malaria, the sense used in public health work
senses.definitionCN: 作为疟疾携带者的这种昆虫，是公共卫生工作中使用的义项
senses.example: Anopheles control cut the local malaria rate sharply.
senses.exampleCN: 按蚊防治使当地疟疾发病率大幅下降。
senses.why: Only this genus transmits human malaria, so in health writing the name stands for the transmission route itself.
senses.whyCN: 只有这一属传播人类疟疾，因此在卫生文献中这个名字就代表传播途径本身。

intro.en: Anopheles is Greek anopheles, useless or harmful, from an-, not, and ophelos, benefit. Meigen fixed it as the genus name in 1818.
intro.cn: anopheles 来自希腊语 anopheles「无用的、有害的」，由 an-「不」与 ophelos「益处」构成。迈根 1818 年把它定为属名。

items.en: Greek an- means not or without before a vowel, the same prefix found in anaerobic and anarchy.
items.cn: 希腊语 an- 在元音前意为「不、没有」，与 anaerobic、anarchy 中的前缀相同。

items.en: Greek ophelos meant benefit, advantage or help, and is related to ophellein, to increase or aid.
items.cn: 希腊语 ophelos 意为「益处、好处、帮助」，与 ophellein「增加、帮助」相关。

items.en: Anopheles therefore meant bringing no benefit, useless, and by extension harmful. It was an evaluative word before it was a name.
items.cn: 因此 anopheles 意为「带不来好处、无用」，引申为「有害」。它先是一个评价词，后来才成为名称。

items.en: Johann Meigen established Anopheles as the genus name in 1818, and the spelling was kept unchanged in English.
items.cn: 迈根 1818 年确立 Anopheles 为属名，英语沿用原拼写未作改动。

items.en: After Ross proved mosquito transmission of malaria in 1897, the name became central to public health, and anopheline is the adjective.
items.cn: 罗斯 1897 年证实疟疾经蚊传播后，这个名字成为公共卫生的核心词，形容词是 anopheline。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against anaphylaxis, a severe allergic reaction; the near-meaning group lists other biting insects and the vector role.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与 anaphylaxis「过敏性休克」混淆；近义组列出其他叮人昆虫与媒介这一角色。

entries.definition: Relating to the anopheles group.
A severe whole-body allergic reaction.
A small plant-sucking insect.
entries.definitionCN: 一种吸食植物汁液的小虫。

entries.definition: Something that departs from the norm.
Any two-winged biting fly of this family.
entries.definitionCN: 该科中任何双翅叮人蝇类。

entries.definition: An organism that carries a pathogen.
A small two-winged flying insect.
A tiny fly, some kinds of which bite.
entries.definitionCN: 一种极小的蝇，部分种类叮人。

normalIntro.en: Anopheles is an- plus ophelos: no benefit, a name that judges the insect rather than describes it.
normalIntro.cn: anopheles 就是 an- 加 ophelos：没有益处，这个名字是在评价这种昆虫，而不是描述它。

normal.en: The word is the same singular and plural: one anopheles, many anopheles.
normal.cn: 单复数同形：one anopheles、many anopheles。

normal.en: The adjective is anopheline, as in anopheline mosquito.
normal.cn: 形容词是 anopheline，如 anopheline mosquito。

normal.en: Only anopheles transmits human malaria, not ordinary house mosquitoes.
normal.cn: 只有按蚊传播人类疟疾，普通家蚊不传播。

normal.en: It rests with the body tilted up, unlike other mosquitoes.
normal.cn: 它停息时身体上翘，与其他蚊子不同。

normal.en: Do not confuse anopheles with anaphylaxis, an allergic reaction.
normal.cn: 别把 anopheles 与 anaphylaxis「过敏反应」混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a thin mosquito leaning back on a leaf.
abstract.cn: 想象一只细瘦的蚊子在叶子上向后倾着身子。

abstract.en: Imagine a shallow puddle full of wriggling larvae.
abstract.cn: 想象一片浅水洼里满是扭动的幼虫。

abstract.en: Think of a name that means no benefit at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一个意为「毫无益处」的名字。

examples.en: Anopheles larvae lie flat on the water surface.
examples.cn: 按蚊幼虫平躺在水面上。

examples.en: The survey mapped every anopheles breeding site.
examples.cn: 调查标出了每一处按蚊繁殖地。

examples.en: An anopheles bite can transmit the malaria parasite.
examples.cn: 按蚊叮咬可传播疟原虫。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：an「无」+ ophel「益处」+ es——对人毫无益处的蚊子，就是按蚊、疟蚊，记住它停着时身子翘起来。

root: 希腊语 an-「无」+ ophelos「益处」构成 anopheles「无用的、有害的」，迈根 1818 年取为蚊属名 Anopheles，因该属传播疟疾而成为公共卫生关键词。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one insect: the genus with its raised posture, and the same insect seen as the route by which malaria travels.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种昆虫：身体上翘的那个蚊属，以及被视为疟疾传播途径的同一种昆虫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin mosquito tilted up beside shallow water
core.cn: 核心意象：浅水边一只翘起身子的细瘦蚊子

branches.en: A mosquito leaning back on a leaf.
branches.cn: 一只在叶子上后倾的蚊子。

branches.en: Larvae lying flat on a puddle.
branches.cn: 平躺在浅水洼上的幼虫。

branches.en: A map of breeding sites to drain.
branches.cn: 一张标出待排干繁殖地的地图。

branches.en: A bite that carries the parasite.
branches.cn: 一次携带病原虫的叮咬。

branches.en: One insect, named then feared.
branches.cn: 同一种昆虫，先被命名，后被畏惧。

intro.en: Anopheles is an- plus ophelos plus -es, and the surrounding vocabulary brings in mal-, aer- and vect-.
intro.cn: anopheles 是 an- 加 ophelos 加 -es，周边词汇还带来 mal-、aer- 与 vect-。

latinIntro.en: The name is wholly Greek: an- and ophelos. It was Latinised only in spelling when Meigen fixed the genus in 1818.
latinIntro.cn: 这个名字完全是希腊语：an- 与 ophelos。迈根 1818 年确立属名时只在拼写上作了拉丁化。

definition_zh: 回答；答复；答案；回（电话、门）；符合
definition_en: to say or write something back to a question, to solve a problem, or to react when someone calls or knocks
core_image: 课堂上举起手，把答案说给老师听
scene: 教室里安静得只剩风扇声，老师看着学生等一个回应。Nobody could answer the last question.
sceneCN: 这里 answer 是「回答」（第 1 个义项：对提问作出回应）；句意是没有人能回答最后那个问题。

pos.zh: 名词：答案；回答；解决办法

derivatives.zh: 形容词：可回答的；负有责任的
动词：回应，是 answer 的拉丁语系近义词

senses.title: To reply to a question
senses.definition: to say or write something in return when someone has asked a question
senses.definitionCN: 当别人提问时，用口头或书面作出回应
senses.example: Nobody could answer the last question.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人能回答最后那个问题。
senses.why: Old English andswaru was built from and, 'against', and swerian, 'to swear', so an answer was originally a statement sworn back against a charge; the backtracking motion of reply is still the core.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 andswaru 由 and「对着」与 swerian「发誓」构成，最初指面对指控时反过来起誓申明，那种「对回去」的动作至今仍是核心。

senses.title: To solve a problem
senses.definition: to work out the solution to a puzzle, a sum, or a difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 算出谜题、算术题的解法，或解决一个难题
senses.example: She answered the riddle in under a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她不到一分钟就解开了这个谜语。
senses.why: A question and a puzzle both leave a gap that must be filled, so the idea of replying widened from words to solutions.
senses.whyCN: 提问与谜题都会留下一个必须填补的空位，所以 answer 从「用话回应」扩展到「给出解法」。

senses.title: To react to a call or knock
senses.definition: to pick up the phone or go to the door when someone is trying to reach you
senses.definitionCN: 有人打来电话或敲门时，去接或去开
senses.example: He answered the phone before the second ring.
senses.exampleCN: 第二声铃响之前他就接了电话。
senses.why: A ringing phone is a question addressed to the house, and picking it up is the physical form of replying.
senses.whyCN: 响铃的电话像是对着屋子里提出的一个问题，而拿起听筒就是把这个回应做成了动作。

senses.title: To fit or correspond to
senses.definition: to match a description, a need, or a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 与某种描述、需要或目的相吻合
senses.example: The room answers the description in every detail.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间在每一处细节上都符合描述。
senses.why: If a thing corresponds to what was asked for, it stands as the reply to the expectation, which is why answer can mean 'fit'.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物正好对应所要求的东西，它就等于对那份期待作出了回应，因此 answer 可以表示「符合」。

intro.en: Answer is a native Germanic compound whose two halves once meant 'against' and 'swear'.
intro.cn: answer 是本族日耳曼语复合词，两部分原本分别表示「对着」与「发誓」。

items.en: and meant 'against' or 'in return', not yet the modern conjunction.
items.cn: and 意为「对着」或「作为回报」，还不是现代的那个连词。

items.en: swerian meant 'to swear an oath'.
items.cn: swerian 意为「起誓」。

items.en: andswaru was a sworn statement made against an accusation.
items.cn: andswaru 指面对指控时起誓作出的申辩。

items.en: The word lost its legal flavour and came to mean any reply.
items.cn: 这个词失去法律色彩，泛指任何答复。

items.en: The noun answer and the verb answer split into separate uses, including answering the phone and answering a need.
items.cn: 名词 answer 与动词 answer 分化出多种用法，包括接电话与满足需要。

note.en: The look-alike group is the answer family; the near-meaning group holds other verbs of replying.
note.cn: 形近组是 answer 词族；近义组是其他表示回应的动词。

left without a reply

normalIntro.en: An answer is something sworn back against a question.
normalIntro.cn: answer 原本就是对着问题「回一句誓词」。

normal.en: Answer the question, answer the phone, answer the door: three everyday pairs.
normal.cn: answer the question、answer the phone、answer the door 是三个常用搭配。

normal.en: The answer to a question uses to, not of.
normal.cn: 「……的答案」用 the answer to，不用 of。

normal.en: Answer for means take responsibility, as in answer for your mistakes.
normal.cn: answer for 意为负责，如 answer for your mistakes。

normal.en: Note the silent w: AN-ser, not an-swer.
normal.cn: 注意 w 不发音：读作 AN-ser。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one spelling.
normal.cn: 名词与动词拼写相同。

abstract.en: See a hand go up in a quiet classroom.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的教室里举起一只手。

abstract.en: See a phone ringing on a wooden desk.
abstract.cn: 想象木桌上响起的电话。

abstract.en: See a key turning in a lock that finally fits.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙终于对上锁孔。

examples.en: Nobody could answer the last question.
examples.cn: 没有人能回答最后那个问题。

examples.en: She answered the riddle in under a minute.
examples.cn: 她不到一分钟就解开了这个谜语。

examples.en: He answered the phone before the second ring.
examples.cn: 第二声铃响之前他就接了电话。

dict_mnemonic.text: an（对着）加 swer（发誓）：对着问题回一句，就是回答。

sensesIntro.en: From spoken reply the word spreads to solving, to answering a call, and to fitting a description.
sensesIntro.cn: 从口头回答出发，这个词扩展到解答问题、接电话应门，以及符合描述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice sent back to the person who asked.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一句话送回提问的人那里。

branches.en: answer a question in class
branches.cn: 在课堂上回答问题

branches.en: answer a letter
branches.cn: 回信

branches.cn: 解开谜语

latinIntro.en: No Latin base underlies answer, so the Latin list is empty.

definition_zh: 蚂蚁；蚁类；蚁群
definition_en: a small insect that lives in large groups in the ground, or the group of such insects as a kind
core_image: 一条细细的黑线在地板上移动，每一粒都是活的小东西
scene: 厨房地板上留下一粒糖，几只小虫排成一线。A single ant carried a crumb across the floor.
sceneCN: 这里 ant 是「蚂蚁」（第 1 个义项：单个蚂蚁）；句意为一只蚂蚁把面包屑搬过地板。画面里有地板、糖粒与排成线的蚂蚁。

derivatives.zh: 由 ant 与 hill 复合，义为「蚁丘；蚁巢」
由 ant 与 eater 复合，义为「食蚁兽」
由 ant 与 like 复合，义为「像蚂蚁一样的」

senses.title: A single small insect
senses.definition: a small insect with a thin waist that lives in an organized colony
senses.definitionCN: 腰部细窄、生活在有组织的蚁群中的小型昆虫
senses.example: An ant crawled up the side of the jar.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蚂蚁沿着罐子的侧面往上爬。
senses.why: Old English named the insect with a word probably meaning 'the biter' or 'the cutter', after its jaws.
senses.whyCN: 古英语给这种昆虫的名字，很可能意为「咬的东西」或「切的东西」，取自它的口器。

senses.title: The species or colony as a group
senses.titleCN: 蚁类；蚁群：作为整体的蚂蚁
senses.definition: the insects of this kind considered as a group, or a colony of them
senses.definitionCN: 把这类昆虫作为一个整体来看，或指一个蚁群
senses.example: The ant is one of the strongest creatures for its size.
senses.exampleCN: 就体型而言，蚂蚁是最强壮的生物之一。
senses.why: A single ant is almost meaningless alone; the word often stands for the colony that behaves like one body.
senses.whyCN: 单只蚂蚁几乎没有独立意义；这个词常代表像一具身体那样行动的整个蚁群。

intro.en: Ant is an Old English word whose modern form lost several sounds and gained an n from the article.
intro.cn: ant 是一个古英语词，现代形式丢掉了几个音，又从冠词那里得到了一个 n。

items.en: Ǣmete named the ant, and related forms appear across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: ǣmete 指蚂蚁，相关形式见于多种日耳曼语言。

items.en: The reconstructed form suggests an original meaning such as 'the biter' or 'the cutter', describing the insect's jaws.
items.cn: 重构形式暗示原义可能是「咬的东西」或「切的东西」，描述这种昆虫的口器。

items.en: Middle English used emmet and ampte; the shorter forms gradually displaced the longer ones.
items.cn: 中古英语用 emmet 与 ampte；较短的形式逐渐取代了较长的形式。

items.en: In phrases such as an emmet, the n of the article could be heard as part of the noun, a process called metanalysis.
items.cn: 在 an emmet 这类短语里，冠词的 n 可能被听成名词的一部分，这一过程称为「重新切分」。

items.en: The modern ant is short and plain, and it now appears in compounds such as anthill and anteater.
items.cn: 现代 ant 简短朴素，如今出现在 anthill 与 anteater 等复合词中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that resemble ant in sound; the near-meaning group gathers small social insects and their kin.
note.cn: 形近组收读音与 ant 相近的短词；近义组收小型社会性昆虫及其近亲。

entries.definition: The sister of one's father or mother.
One of the branched horns of a deer.
An animal that feeds mainly on ants.
entries.definitionCN: 主要以蚂蚁为食的动物。

entries.definition: The broad class of small six-legged creatures.
A small pale insect that eats wood and lives in colonies.
entries.definitionCN: 吃木头、群居生活的小型浅色昆虫。

entries.definition: A flying insect that collects nectar and lives in hives.
entries.definitionCN: 采集花蜜、住在蜂巢里的飞行昆虫。

entries.definition: An insect with hard wing cases.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the lost n, the short sound, and the picture of a line of tiny carriers.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子用到丢掉的 n、短促的读音，以及「一列小小搬运工」的画面。

normal.en: Say 'ant': one short syllable, as small as the insect.
normal.cn: 读作「ant」，一个短音节，和那只昆虫一样小。

normal.en: It rhymes with pant and chant, which makes the short a easy to hold.
normal.cn: 它与 pant、chant 押韵，短 a 音很容易记住。

normal.en: The old word was emmet, and the n drifted over from 'an emmet'.
normal.cn: 古词是 emmet，n 是从「an emmet」那里漂过来的。

normal.en: An anthill is an ant hill, and an anteater eats ants; the compounds tell the story.
normal.cn: anthill 是蚂蚁的丘，anteater 是吃蚂蚁的兽；复合词自己会讲故事。

normal.en: One ant is tiny; a colony of ants can carry a whole leaf.
normal.cn: 一只蚂蚁很小，一群蚂蚁却能搬走整片叶子。

abstract.en: The ant is proof that a small body can do large work when it is not alone.
abstract.cn: 蚂蚁证明了：小身体只要不孤单，也能做大事。

abstract.en: We notice the single ant only when it is already a line.
abstract.cn: 我们注意到那只蚂蚁时，它往往已经排成了一条线。

abstract.en: The word is small, and most of what it means is the colony behind it.
abstract.cn: 这个词很小，而它含义的大部分是背后的蚁群。

examples.en: An ant can lift several times its own weight.
examples.cn: 一只蚂蚁能举起自身体重数倍的东西。

examples.en: The ants found the sugar within minutes.
examples.cn: 蚂蚁几分钟内就找到了糖。

examples.en: He watched a line of ants cross the path.
examples.cn: 他看着一列蚂蚁穿过小路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安特」：安特趴在地上看蚂蚁，一看就是一下午。

root: 古英语 ǣmete（蚂蚁），源自日耳曼语，原义可能与「咬、切」有关；现代拼写受冠词重新切分影响。

sensesIntro.en: The word names one small insect and also the colony or kind as a whole.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词既指一只小昆虫，也指作为整体的蚁群或蚁类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single tiny body moving in a line of identical bodies.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具微小的身体，在由相同身体排成的队列中移动。

branches.en: THE INDIVIDUAL: the first sense is one insect.
branches.cn: 个体线：第一个义项是一只昆虫。

branches.en: THE COLONY: the second sense is the group acting as one.
branches.cn: 群体线：第二个义项是作为一个整体行动的蚁群。

branches.en: THE LINE: one ant becomes visible only as part of a moving line.
branches.cn: 队列线：一只蚂蚁只有成为移动队列的一部分时才显眼。

branches.en: THE LOAD: a single ant carries a crumb, and the colony carries the whole store.
branches.cn: 负重线：单蚁搬一粒屑，蚁群搬整个粮仓。

branches.en: THE KIND: the word can stand for the species as a whole, as in the ant.
branches.cn: 种类线：这个词可代表整个蚁类，如 the ant。

intro.en: Ant forms compounds with hill, eater and like, and with roles inside the colony.
intro.cn: ant 与 hill、eater、like 以及蚁群内的角色构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; the compounds are English, though the second elements may come from Latin or French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语；复合词为英语所造，后半部分可能来自拉丁语或法语。

items.exampleCN: 孩子们跨过一个低矮的蚁丘。

items.meaning: an animal that feeds on ants

items.exampleCN: 食蚁兽有一条长长的黏舌。
